chapterTitle: Chapter 1: The Winged Whales resting ground (Ceres)
editorText:
The date is SOL year 2056

A bright splintering light etched it’s way into John’s retina’s behind his closed eyelids, as cold quarts glass pressed against his cheek. The paining ceiling light reflection on the outer layer of the porthole assured him his spirit was not floating in the cold void of space. For a moment he questioned his sanity, as he rose from what felt like and exhausting dream, Deprived of proper rest, his alarm pierced his ears as a voice emitted over his personal comms implant, “Deep space training to commence in an hour at 0700, captain. I’ll inform the others to meet you in the mess hall. Have a good morning, captain.” John slowly lifted his restless body, leaning forward from his bunk, gazing out at the stars. “Ahh.., Kitten, one more thing, I heard that they uploaded a new breakfast print. What's all the fuss?” Static followed by a sweet voice chirped, “Oh yes, captain, the latest update is guava-flavoured tofu with salted raw sliced salmon.” John grunted, “Yeah, pass. They keep trying to get that right, but fish that doesn’t taste right, well, it just ain’t right in any capacity if you ask me.” Kitten emitted a small electronic chuckle. “Noted, captain.”

Making his way toward the docking bay transport pods, John imagined himself walking through the rib cage of a giant winged whale. Curvilinear structural pillars rose with smooth contours from the skirtings, Balaenoptera’s concave hull design was intended to deflect incoming projectiles, however as she had never seen battle since her commission. This costly design only served to project the Balaenoptera’s Majesty signaling her place as the protectant flagship. John carried an almost ethereal presence, a tangible aura of gentle authority, as he decisively traversed the disproportionately quiet halls passing by the occasional colleague. For a brief moment, the world seemed to slow down in his tread. Those who caught even a fleeting glimpse of the captain felt entranced, their gazes filled with reverent curiosity. John, a man of few acquaintances among the crowd, couldn't help but wonder about the intricate tapestry of destinies that would soon unfold during the long awaited supply voyage to Europa; each stranger's life a unique thread in the grand design of the human expansion into the skeptics universe. Perhaps it was this inherent curiosity and care for his companion’s; for human life which led John to carry out his actions, which consequently solidified into folk tale amongst the flock. John’s uniform was never quite perfect, a cuff loosely amiss, a button haphazardly stray. People couldn't pin why he stalled so long in his rank as captain. whispers within the ranks about his commitment to his comrades dismissed any doubts. People hoped they might one day gain the unspoken respect the captain conjured. They understood that where a button strayed Indiscreetly, John made up for it with every aspect when in field kit. He drilled his team as if their kit were a ceremonial uniform, one they would hopefully in John’s eyes, never have to wear to their funeral. To John, an ill-prepared kit meant death. A uniform didn't get you home; it got you through the halls, through the formalities, not the field. John allowed his team some slack. Those passing nodded to the captain in respect. John detested salutes, but welcomed camaraderie; these things meant more to him than forced compliance.

At the end of Balaenoptera’s main hall, a seamless but large opening recessed into the wall; conveniently placed just before the bridge. “Commander Marcellus Athos” Etched in an almost Roman calligraphy, Bronze Capitals brazed across glistening black oxide blast doors, John felt himself die a little bit inside just that bit more at the chauvinism of it all. As he veered to the right to enter the grav lift to the mess hall, the fine calligraphy began to make way, retracting into the double layered blast walls of the hall as the doors gave way. “Commander Athos” John remarked head tilted slightly forward, hands tucked effortlessly behind his ever so slightly, now straighter back. Johns fingers slowly finessed a strayed cuff button back into it’s holder. “Walker!” Marcellus proclaimed! “Just the man I wanted to see, headed to the mess so soon?”, “Fuck. first that weird fucking dream, now I have to contend with this guy” John thought to himself. “I hear the salmon guava is.. off world” said John in a sarcastic tone. Marcellus’s eyes met with John’s. “Precisely, we can’t have Europa’s new workers having acquired tastes now can we” John eased his foot forward in sync with the Commanders toward the bridge; shoulder to shoulder they paced through the thick blast doors as they gave way to the majesty of the bridge.

The Baelenoptera’s bridge was usually a hive of activity whilst under-way, but she was now docked with Ceres and her crew enjoyed the rare comfort of social norms with the station's inhabitants. The Commander had made the bridge his personal, informal meeting room. streamlined along the bridge walls, arrays of data charts projected color mapped “estimated” unrest in regions across the Earth’s face. This made John Anxious, observing the color array he knew how quick it could mean a fast burn to deploying halfway across the globe.

“A flavor modeled on the samples taken from the minerals within Europa’s water; Ceres home committee thought it might give the new workers a taste of what’s to come” John chuckled under his breath “Strange way of enticing the crew to the journey ahead wouldn’t you say Commander” Marcellus stopped abruptly before the bridge control panel. “What would you advise builds resilience in people, Walker?” said Athos. John's eyes lifted from the luminous holographic slingshot vectors pathing way to Europa, floating in the center of the room, moving from the peaceful hum of the stellar map, to meet Marcellus’s anxiously waiting gaze. “These people have already sacrificed and given up their homes and half of them their families back on earth, the least we can do is accommodate them with something that feels like home, at least until they know what that is”

Marcellus let out a heavy Sigh, then continued in a persuasive tone at John “Plants have been shown to have higher survival rates post transplant to different environments with slow environmental progressions, humans are much the same.” John slowly paced the bridge observing the charts trying to draw conclusions on where he and his team might be posted to next.  “They only have a short time in orbit with preparations before they are fully committed, better to thin the herd of dead weight wouldn’t you agree… before sending them on the full leg”.

John had thought this grand coming from someone who didn’t even eat in the general mess with the crew. He gazed down on Ceres station looking over the foreboding nose of the Balaenoptera. Ceres, short for the Collective Earthwide Reconciliation Endeavour Settlement, was the result of a global  wide effort to forward the boundaries of space exploration and resource acquisition. In its orbital rotation the shimmering edge of the Earth waking from the darkness of space had a disorienting effect to freshly seasoned spacers.

Coupled with the name of the Greek Goddess of agriculture and cultivation, Ceres was a mother structure, a labyrinth of separate winding modules and docking stations which formed the crust of an internal womb shielded from the cold of space. CERES began as an experiment for deep space agricultural cultivation, eventually as the project gained traction in its success it quickly became the first space workers settlement growing in size, the inner layers like records of past technological progression, preserved conservatively in respect to the scarcity of earth's resources.

Perplexed by the advancements and in such short time made by the CERES project, John couldn’t help but raise the question to Marcellus, “I understand the CLEAR program guides us and has aided us in getting this far, but the workers seem uneasy with how invested the model has been for so long with it’s self driven development, there are rumours in certain circles of a rogue group which seeks to manipulate the core algorithm to their own agenda, people are getting impatient, and they want better working conditions, cleaner air, more regularly replaced filters, cleaner water. It’s turning into a mess down there, morale markers have shown to decline in recent years, and you are pressing strange cuisine on them. these are sensitive times Marcellus, can we really afford to be messing with an already frustrated and agitated populous”

“Hmmm yes John, these are trying times. I still remember the fall of the world bank, it took time for the economy to take its roots again within the monetary reform, but the sacrifices paid off didn’t they? have faith in the program John, we haven’t seen war in over a century now, before long it will be a dusty drive in the archive. The models self investment is a delicate situation, Keynes envisioned that technology would result in a surplus economy, and now we must let that path take its course, something we need to exercise carefully, with these cautionary measures sometimes there are certain setbacks, I’m sure you understand” Marcellus gently conveyed his view with sincerity in his voice, but a firm eye. John let out a shallow breath, he agreed with the man, however pushed back gently “I see what you are getting at, however I can help but feel that the algorithm is only as good as the data which is fed into it. If our engineers don’t cater for an increase in population and workforce on Ceres, or the over expansion of that economy, fluctuations in weather and real world events. The model is good and I won’t deny it has stamped out corruption, but it isn’t perfect, we still have a long way to go''.

Marcellus listened with a clear conscience, his finger pressed on his chin resting upon his palm, elbow tucked on his hip. Marcellus was swift in his response. “Your humble yet considerate approach on situations is why I keep you around Walker, I believe I can count on you to keep a watchful eye on things, while my attention is not always on the real world but the scientific advancements for the new world.. I know I can count on you, in-fact after this next mission, I think it might be time you hung up your field suit for a more safeguarded role in a political uniform; I think you have a heart for Techracy, you might help the algorithm see evolving issues that it had not yet considered”. John was surprised by Marcellus' offer, he respected his thoughtful gesture, meeting his offer with a reserved acceptance, “You know it would be nice to hang up the kit, politics hasn’t always been my forte, at least in Techracy I could patch up a few holes beyond my reach.. Thanks for the consideration Marcellus, I may take you up on that one day, but for now seeing the issues first hand helps me get a first base view. what is this mission you whispered of?”.

Marcellus took a deep breath as he paced the bridge port window, looking out over Ceres, across the bustling crowds of Technicians, Technocrats, and protectants pacing to their respective roles. The faces of Technicians wandered with heavy eyes through the halls, a feeling of disgruntlement strewn across their frowns and occasional reluctant smiles.  'This mission is of the utmost secrecy, John,' Marcellus said, his voice low and measured. 'I know this goes against all we have strived for in transparency with the broader public, although we can’t risk the civil unrest should remnants of our past be found as the cause of this anomaly. Do you understand what is at stake here..” the room fell silent for a moment, John seemed lost and confused deep in thought, “John?' John gave a steady nod; masked beneath this physical formal agreement, his true thoughts and distrust firmly concealed behind a wall of silence. “Ok well I am glad we cleared that up” Marcellus proceeded to discuss the details of the mission.

“For almost 5 decades now we have been picking up low band frequency signals we assumed were just random static, recently the signal has become more pronounced, and we have been able to tri-laterate the location of these transmissions from stations positioned on several moons throughout the solar system. The transmissions seem to point to general areas in the outer orbital paths of sol’s planets; these signals get stronger peculiarly with each planet's orbital rotation. We haven’t been able to confirm if this is true for the outer planets yet, but the locations seem to form a trajectory. Recently we have observed stronger signal amplitude, although we can’t actually interpret what this signal is, as it seems to be encrypted. The amplitude spiked recently when a distress beacon was detected on Earth, in the northern region of Nepal deep within the Himalayan mountains. Your team is to investigate and report back. Locate the source of the signal, extract any information and data you can then once you are certain, send coordinates and terrain scans for extraction.. You know the drill”. “Data extraction. Got it”, John seemed unphased really.

“Keep your wits about you John” Marcellus cut in.  “There are records of independent groups operating in the area, but our long range scanners can’t detect anything due to the density of the atmosphere. You’ll be blind, but at best I would advise caution and to expect possible hostilities.” Said Athos, grimly, yet with an uncanny confidence in his voice. John thought it quite apathetic, but shrugged it off internally. “I wonder how invested he is in this facility.. if he has lost site of the expansion cause” Walker thought to himself. Then like water running past his ears, he was brought back into the room. “Yes” shot walker, with extremely subtle sarcasm, “Hostiles” he let out in a medium tone, followed with a look of authoritative submission, not reassuring enough to Athos that he felt John on his side, but enough assurance, or so through his clean record. Little did he know. “Ok John.. I’ll leave it in your capable hands”

Athos turned his shoulder to john, looking out over the station through the bridge window, his silence with a gentle permeating respect, “At ease” permitting him to leave the room.
